t: Timur, a Barlas noble from Transoxiana, carved out an empire from Anatolia to the borders of China by conquest and calculated terror.
His heirs turned Samarkand and Herat into brilliant centres of painting, poetry and astronomy that shaped Safavid and Mughal culture.
Built on one man's authority, it split among feuding princes after 1405 and fell to the Uzbeks, but Babur carried its legacy to Mughal India.
dyk: Ulugh Beg's Samarkand star catalogue of over a thousand stars was among the most accurate before the telescope, and was published at Oxford in 1665.
ev: Timur's army raises towers of skulls from the population of Isfahan
Timur defeats Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde on the Terek
Timur sacks Delhi, leaving the city devastated for decades
Timur defeats and captures the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I at Ankara
Timur dies at Otrar while marching to invade Ming China
Ulugh Beg is put to death at the instigation of his own son
Abu Sa'id, last Timurid to reunite much of the realm, is killed fighting the Aq Qoyunlu
Muhammad Shaybani Khan takes Herat, ending Timurid rule
